description: Iranian nationals must pay a departure tax before passport control, rising by trip number within the solar year: 1st ﷼9,000,000, 2nd ﷼15,000,000, 3rd ﷼22,000,000. Payable online in advance or at Bank Melli branches, with the slip shown to the passport police. Religious travel is taxed far less on second and subsequent departures.
energy_note: Leaving repeatedly is priced as suspicious behaviour.
notes: Rial figures move with budget cycles - verify before quoting.

description: A further levy added in 2024 applies to all passengers over two years old, is calculated at a government-controlled exchange rate, and exempts pilgrims to Iraq, Saudi Arabia and Syria. It sits on top of the ordinary duty - about 520,000 rials (roughly USD 8.80) for the year to March 2025.

Up to EUR 5,000 equivalent in cash or bank documents; above that needs Central Bank approval. Up to 150g of gold, silver or platinum jewellery and 3kg of non-antique silver. Iranian gold coins are prohibited from export under any circumstances. Up to 24 square metres of hand-woven carpet, 125g caviar, 150g saffron.
energy_note: A life's savings capped at what fits in a pocket.

description: Gold coins are the standard Iranian household savings instrument precisely because the currency is unstable - and they are the one thing absolutely barred from leaving.
energy_note: The savings vehicle that cannot emigrate with you.

aspect: Tax clearance as an exit condition
description: For foreigners, an exit visa typically requires a tax clearance certificate; failure to obtain one can result in travel restrictions and penalties. Tax residency arises after 183 days.

Hassan's savings are 40 Bahar Azadi gold coins, held since 2014 because the rial is not a savings vehicle. Coins may not be exported under any circumstances. He can take 150g of jewellery. He sells the coins at a bad rate to a dealer who knows he is leaving, and carries the loss out as a rounding error.
money_note: Distress-sale discount on the family savings.
energy_note: A lifetime of saving, discounted for being in a hurry.
